items.followUp: Name the two transport systems in humans and state one substance transported by each.

rubric.why: The two systems of materials transport in humans are identified.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct system named.

modelAnswer: The two systems of materials transport in humans are the circulatory system and the lymphatic system.

items.followUp: Where is pericardial fluid found, and how does it help the heart?

rubric.why: Identifies the location of the fluid around the heart.
rubric.description: States where pericardial fluid is found.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is between the layers of the pericardium.

rubric.why: States the fluid’s function during heart movement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it reduces friction as the heart beats.

modelAnswer: Pericardial fluid is the fluid present between the two layers of the pericardium surrounding the heart.
It reduces friction between these layers as the heart beats.

items.followUp: Explain the tissue, organ and organ-system levels of organization, giving an example of an organ system.

rubric.why: Explains that an organ consists of tissues working together to perform a function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an organ as a structure made of different tissues and 1 mark for their coordinated function.

rubric.why: Explains that organs work together as an organ system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an organ system is a group of organs and 1 mark for their coordinated function or a suitable example.

modelAnswer: At the organ level, different tissues are joined and work together to perform a particular function; for example, the stomach is an organ.
At the organ-system level, several organs work together to perform a major function of the body.
For example, the digestive system consists of organs such as the mouth, stomach and intestines, which work together in digestion.

items.followUp: Name the three main types of plastids and state the function of each.

rubric.why: Identifies plastids as structures found in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing plastids as organelles or structures found in plant cells.

rubric.why: Identifies the green plastid and its role in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chloroplasts, chlorophyll and photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Identifies coloured plastids and their pigments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain coloured pigments or give colour to plant parts.

rubric.why: Identifies colourless plastids and their storage role.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that leucoplasts are colourless and store food.

rubric.why: Gives examples of substances stored by leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one stored material, such as starch, oil or protein.

modelAnswer: Plastids are organelles found in the cytoplasm of plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers and fruits.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food such as starch, oils and proteins.

items.followUp: What are enzymes? Give one example of their use in the food industry and one in detergents.

rubric.why: Defines enzymes by their role in speeding up reactions in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzymes as biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.

rubric.why: Gives a relevant food-industry use of enzymes.
rubric.description: Explains an enzyme use in the food industry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as enzymes in baking, cheese-making or meat tenderising.

rubric.why: Explains how enzymes are used in detergents.
rubric.description: Explains an enzyme use in detergents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes help break down stains in detergents.

rubric.why: Gives an additional industrial use of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable additional example, such as textile or leather processing.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms.
In the food industry, enzymes are used in baking, cheese-making or meat tenderising.
In detergent manufacture, enzymes help break down stains.
Enzymes are also used in industries such as textile and leather processing.

items.followUp: Explain how farming contributes to the production of food and other useful products.

rubric.why: Identifies farming as the growing or cultivation of crops.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that farming involves cultivating or growing crops.

rubric.why: States a useful product or outcome of farming.
rubric.description: Gives the importance or products of farming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning food, useful plant products such as fibre, or animal products from livestock.

modelAnswer: Farming is the profession of cultivating crops and rearing animals.
It provides food and useful products such as fibre, and may also provide products from livestock.

items.followUp: Write the scientific name of mustard and give two uses of the plant.

rubric.why: Gives the scientific name used for mustard.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct scientific name.

rubric.why: Gives uses of mustard, such as its oil and seeds used as a spice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two valid uses, for example oil for cooking and seeds used as a spice or condiment.

modelAnswer: The scientific name of mustard is Brassica campestris.
Mustard seeds are used to obtain oil, and they are also used as a spice or condiment.

items.followUp: State one difference between the scientific method and the biological method.

rubric.why: Shows that the scientific method is a general approach used to investigate problems in different fields.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the scientific method is a general, systematic way of investigating problems.

rubric.why: Shows that the biological method applies scientific investigation to biological problems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the biological method is used to investigate problems in biology.

modelAnswer: The scientific method is a general, systematic way of investigating problems in any field.
The biological method is the application of systematic investigation to problems in biology.
